checkpoints.title: Address ranges are determined by prefix length
checkpoints.prompt: Divide 10.0.0.0/24 into /26 subnets. Select one correct statement.

choices.text: Each /26 has 64 addresses and can be placed contiguously
choices.explanation: Correct.

choices.text: Each /26 has 256 addresses and overlaps
choices.explanation: /26 has 64 addresses.

choices.text: Changing the prefix length does not change the address range.
choices.explanation: It determines the length of the host portion.

checkpoints.title: Keep subnets within the VPC and avoid overlap
checkpoints.prompt: Divide VPC 10.0.0.0/24 into 10.0.0.0/25 and 10.0.0.128/25. Select one correct verification.

choices.text: Verify that both are within the VPC and do not overlap each other
choices.explanation: Correct.

choices.text: Overlap is resolved by route table priority
choices.explanation: Overlapping subnet CIDRs are not allowed.

choices.text: Determine containment by name alone
choices.explanation: Verify using the numeric ranges.

checkpoints.title: Determine capacity after subtracting AWS-reserved IP addresses
checkpoints.prompt: Use an AWS IPv4 /28 subnet. Select one correct estimate of the number of available addresses.

choices.text: Subtract the 5 reserved addresses from 16
choices.explanation: Correct.

choices.text: Assign all 16 addresses to EC2
choices.explanation: Reserved IP addresses must be excluded.

choices.text: The number of reserved addresses is determined by the number of route tables
choices.explanation: Reservations are a rule for IPv4 subnets.

checkpoints.title: Verify the conditions for external connectivity
checkpoints.prompt: The EC2 instance has a public IPv4 address, but there is no IGW route in the subnet's route table. Choose one correct judgment.

choices.text: A public IPv4 address alone does not satisfy the conditions for Internet reachability.
choices.explanation: Correct. A route to an IGW is also required.

choices.text: A route can be created using only a NACL.
choices.explanation: A NACL evaluates permissions; it does not create routes.

choices.text: Changing the CIDR eliminates the need for an IGW.
choices.explanation: External reachability requires an appropriate gateway route.

choices.text: /26 is a narrower range than /24
choices.explanation: Correct. /26 has 6 host bits and contains 64 addresses.

choices.text: /26 is a broader range than /24
choices.explanation: The longer the prefix length, the narrower the address range.

choices.text: The prefix represents a port number.
choices.explanation: The number after the slash in CIDR is the number of bits in the network portion.

finalQuestions.prompt: A network administrator is comparing IPv4 CIDR blocks, 10.0.0.0/24 and 10.0.0.0/26, with the same starting address. Select one correct statement about the relationship between the two address ranges.
finalQuestions.title: Prefix and Range

choices.explanation: /25 divides it into two equal parts.
Correct. It divides it into four equal parts of 64 addresses each.
It does not divide the range.

finalQuestions.prompt: A designer wants to divide the 10.0.0.0/24 assigned to a VPC entirely into four non-overlapping subnets of equal size. Select one correct prefix length for each subnet.
finalQuestions.title: Four Equal Parts

choices.text: /24 represents 256 IPv4 addresses
choices.explanation: It is 2 to the 8th power.

choices.text: /26 represents 64 IPv4 addresses
choices.explanation: It is 2 to the 6th power.

choices.text: Two consecutive /26 blocks have the same range as /24
choices.explanation: Two adjacent /26 blocks contain 128 addresses in total. This range corresponds to /25 and does not constitute the entire 256-address /24 range.

finalQuestions.prompt: A designer assigned 10.0.0.0/26 and 10.0.0.64/26 within 10.0.0.0/24. When determining whether the remainder can be used for another subnet, select one incorrect statement about IPv4 CIDR.
finalQuestions.title: Calculating the Range

choices.text: Verify that the candidate CIDR is within the VPC CIDR
choices.explanation: A subnet must be contained within the VPC.

choices.text: The same CIDR can be used if the AZs are different
choices.explanation: Correct. Subnet CIDRs within the same VPC cannot overlap, regardless of the AZ.

choices.text: Compare the starting and ending addresses to check for overlap
choices.explanation: Check the numeric ranges.

finalQuestions.prompt: A network administrator is creating subnets in two Availability Zones of the same VPC. When assigning an IPv4 CIDR to each subnet, select one incorrect statement.
finalQuestions.title: No Overlap

choices.explanation: Because it is contained in 10.0.0.0/25, it overlaps with the existing subnet.
It is outside the existing /25 and fits within the VPC.
It is outside the existing /25 and fits within the VPC.
It does not fit within the VPC’s 10.0.0.0/24, so it cannot be assigned to this VPC.

finalQuestions.prompt: A designer is adding a new /26 subnet to the VPC IPv4 CIDR 10.0.0.0/24. 10.0.0.0/25 is already in use. Select two incorrect candidates for the addition.
finalQuestions.title: Additional Subnets

choices.text: Be completely contained within the VPC CIDR
choices.explanation: Correct.

choices.text: Not overlap with existing subnets
choices.explanation: Correct.

choices.text: Have a subnet name different from existing names
choices.explanation: A name does not eliminate CIDR overlap.

choices.text: Have a separate route table
choices.explanation: A route table does not determine whether a CIDR is valid.

finalQuestions.prompt: A network administrator is assigning another subnet to a VPC while keeping the existing subnets. Select two conditions that the candidate IPv4 CIDR must satisfy.
finalQuestions.title: Planning Order

choices.explanation: Five addresses are reserved.
Correct. Subtract the 5 reserved addresses from 64.
Incorrect because the first 4 addresses and the last address are reserved.

finalQuestions.prompt: A design engineer uses a regular IPv4 /26 subnet with an address range allocated by AWS. Excluding the addresses reserved by AWS, how many IPv4 addresses can be assigned to resources? Select one correct number.
finalQuestions.title: Reserved IPs

choices.text: Add the AWS-reserved IPs to the required number and choose the CIDR
choices.explanation: Correct. Base the decision on the number of usable addresses.

choices.text: Because /27 has 32 addresses, 50 can be used if the reserved addresses are ignored
choices.explanation: There are not enough addresses even in the total.

choices.text: Check the 59 usable addresses in /26 and the available headroom
choices.explanation: Correct.

choices.text: Exclude reserved IPs from the design because they are needed only during communication
choices.explanation: They cannot be assigned, so they must be included in the plan.

finalQuestions.prompt: A platform engineer plans to use up to 50 IPv4 addresses in a subnet. The amount of future growth is uncertain. Select two actions to take before deciding on the size of the new subnet.
finalQuestions.title: Capacity Planning

choices.text: Assign a reserved IP as an EC2 address when addresses are insufficient
choices.explanation: Correct. Reserved IPs generally cannot be assigned to resources.

choices.text: Estimate the required CIDR including the number of reserved IPs
choices.explanation: This allows the number of usable addresses to be determined correctly.

choices.text: The number of reserved addresses affects CIDR capacity planning
choices.explanation: They reduce the number of usable addresses.

finalQuestions.prompt: In an active VPC, an operations engineer is investigating a shortage of IPv4 addresses. Regarding addresses reserved by AWS in a subnet, select one incorrect action.
finalQuestions.title: Handling Reservations

choices.text: The subnet route table has an outbound route to the IGW
choices.explanation: Correct. The IGW is the route target.

choices.text: EC2 has a public IPv4 address or an Elastic IP
choices.explanation: Correct. This is required for IPv4 reachability through the IGW.

choices.text: The subnet name is public
choices.explanation: A name does not determine reachability.

choices.text: The CIDR is 10.0.0.0/24
choices.explanation: The CIDR numbers alone do not determine public accessibility.

finalQuestions.prompt: A web administrator accepts direct HTTPS connections over IPv4 from users on the internet to EC2. Application listening and communication permissions are already configured. Select two required address and routing conditions.
finalQuestions.title: Public Access Requirements

choices.text: Check the IGW route in the relevant route table
choices.explanation: This verifies the reachability conditions.

choices.text: Do not check the route table because the subnet name is public
choices.explanation: Correct. The name is not evidence.

choices.text: Check permission for port 443 and the service listener
choices.explanation: These are necessary conditions other than routing.

choices.text: Look only at the CIDR and do not check the port or listener
choices.explanation: Correct. The CIDR alone does not satisfy the connection requirements.

finalQuestions.prompt: An operations administrator is investigating why an internet user cannot connect via HTTPS to a web application on EC2 with a public IPv4 address. Select two incorrect investigation approaches.
finalQuestions.title: Investigating Inability to Access Publicly

choices.text: Place only the necessary entry points on public routes and design the outbound requirements of the other tiers separately
choices.explanation: It is appropriate to limit the public entry points and consider outbound communication for internal tiers separately.

choices.text: A security group is unnecessary if an IGW route exists
choices.explanation: Routing and communication permissions are separate conditions.

choices.text: The name private alone can prevent external access
choices.explanation: Routes, addresses, and permissions must be checked.

choices.text: Provide public routes for the web tier and allow only the necessary internal communication for the database tier.
choices.explanation: This limits direct user connections to the web tier and avoids exposing the database tier.

finalQuestions.prompt: An architect is placing three tiers—a public web tier, an internal application tier, and a database tier—in a VPC. Only the web tier should accept direct connections from the internet. Select two incorrect judgments regarding this requirement.
finalQuestions.title: Layer Exposure Scope

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.text: Read CIDR as an address range and determine separately whether ranges overlap, how many addresses can be assigned, and what conditions are required for communication with the internet.

blocks.label: Learning objective
blocks.text: Plan non-overlapping subnets within a VPC and explain the required capacity and public access conditions with supporting reasons.

blocks.label: Learning objectives
blocks.text: Explain the relationship between prefix length and the range of IPv4 addresses.

blocks.label: Learning objectives
blocks.text: Determine whether a subnet range fits within the VPC and does not overlap with existing subnets.

blocks.label: Learning objectives
blocks.text: Estimate the number of available addresses, including AWS-reserved IP addresses.

blocks.label: Learning objective
blocks.text: You can determine public reachability from routes and addresses rather than names.

blocks.label: The address range is determined by the prefix length
blocks.text: In IPv4 CIDR notation, /24 indicates that the first 24 bits are the network portion. The remaining 8 bits can represent 256 addresses. With /26, 6 bits remain, so there are 64 addresses. The longer the prefix length, the smaller the address range.

blocks.label: The address range is determined by the prefix length
blocks.text: To divide 10.0.0.0/24 into four equal parts, the boundaries are /26 blocks of 64 addresses each. Verify them using the start and end of each range, such as 10.0.0.0/26, 10.0.0.64/26, 10.0.0.128/26, and 10.0.0.192/26.

blocks.label: The address range is determined by the prefix length
blocks.text: CIDR represents numeric ranges, not names. Before adding a VPC or subnet, check that it fits within the parent range and does not overlap an existing range.

steps.label: The address range is determined by the prefix length

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: Divide VPC 10.0.0.0/24 into four subnets of equal size.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Divide the 256 addresses in /24 by 4 and calculate 64 addresses for each.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Assign /26 to each subnet.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: List the start and end addresses, and check for omissions and overlaps.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: You can verify the division from the size and boundaries of the ranges without memorizing prefix lengths.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: Because /26 has a larger number than /24, it represents a wider range.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: The prefix length is the length of the network portion. Because /26 has fewer host bits, it represents a narrower range than /24.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: The longer the prefix length, the smaller the address range.

blocks.label: Key point
blocks.text: Check the range by verifying its start and end.

blocks.label: Keep subnets within the VPC and avoid overlap
blocks.text: A subnet CIDR must be fully contained within the VPC CIDR and must not overlap with another subnet in the same VPC. This condition does not change even when the AZs are different.

blocks.label: Keep subnets within the VPC and avoid overlap
blocks.text: In VPC 10.0.0.0/24, which already uses 10.0.0.0/25, you cannot add 10.0.0.64/26 because it is contained within the existing range. In contrast, 10.0.0.128/26 is adjacent to the existing /25 and does not overlap.

blocks.label: Keep subnets within the VPC and avoid overlap
blocks.text: Route tables and subnet names do not eliminate CIDR overlap. Design the numerical ranges first, then decide the AZ placement and routing.

steps.label: Keep subnets within the VPC and avoid overlap

blocks.label: Scenario
blocks.text: In VPC 10.0.0.0/24, create an application subnet in addition to the existing 10.0.0.0/25.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Confirm that the candidate CIDR is within VPC 10.0.0.0/24.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Compare its start and end range with the existing /25.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Choose a non-overlapping candidate such as 10.0.0.128/26.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: You can determine whether it is allowed based on CIDR containment and overlap, without relying on AZ names or route tables.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: If they are in different AZs, the same CIDR can be reused for two subnets.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: Within the same VPC, subnet CIDRs cannot overlap regardless of the AZs.

blocks.label: Takeaway
blocks.text: Check containment within the parent CIDR first.

blocks.label: Takeaway
blocks.text: Overlaps cannot be resolved by routes.

blocks.label: Determine capacity after subtracting AWS-reserved IP addresses
blocks.text: In AWS IPv4 subnets, the first four and the last one, for a total of five IP addresses, are reserved. A /24 has 251 of 256 addresses, and a /26 has 59 of 64 addresses available for ordinary resources.

blocks.label: Determine capacity after subtracting AWS-reserved IP addresses
blocks.text: Choosing the smallest CIDR based only on the required number of EC2 instances can leave you short because of reserved IP addresses and growth. Add together the required number of network interfaces, addresses used by AWS services, and future headroom before choosing the prefix length.

blocks.label: Determine capacity after subtracting AWS-reserved IP addresses
blocks.text: Reserved IP addresses do not change based on route tables or port numbers. Distinguish the available count from the total count, and document the assumptions in the design.

steps.label: Determine capacity after subtracting AWS-reserved IP addresses

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: Choose a subnet for a workload that uses up to 50 IPv4 addresses.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Determine that a /27, with 32 addresses in total, is insufficient even before reservations.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Subtract the 5 reserved addresses from the 64 total addresses in a /26.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Check whether the 59 available addresses leave enough room for future growth.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: You can plan capacity using the available addresses without carrying an address shortage over to deployment time.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: Because /26 contains 64 addresses, all 64 can necessarily be assigned to EC2 instances.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: In an AWS IPv4 subnet, 5 addresses are reserved, so /26 normally provides 59 usable addresses.

blocks.label: Key takeaways
blocks.text: The total number of addresses and the number of available addresses are different.

blocks.label: Key takeaways
blocks.text: Include reserved IP addresses and room for growth in your planning.

blocks.label: Verify the conditions for external connectivity
blocks.text: Determine whether a subnet has a route to an internet gateway by checking its route table association. The fact that the CIDR is 10.0.0.0/24 or that the subnet is named “public” alone does not determine whether it is public.

blocks.label: Verify the conditions for external connectivity
blocks.text: To make an instance reachable from the internet over IPv4, you must have a route to the IGW, assign a public IPv4 address or Elastic IP to the target network interface, and allow the required traffic through a security group or equivalent controls.

steps.label: Verify the conditions for external connectivity

blocks.label: Check the conditions for external connectivity
blocks.text: To avoid inadvertently exposing the layer where applications or data reside, place only the necessary entry points on the public path. Design outbound communication from private layers separately, using NAT gateways, VPC endpoints, or other options as required.

steps.label: Check the conditions for external connectivity

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: External HTTPS connections to the EC2 instance in the subnet named "public" are failing.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: In the subnet's route table, verify that the route with destination 0.0.0.0/0 points to the IGW.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Verify that the EC2 instance has a public IPv4 address or an Elastic IP.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Verify the minimum required permission for TCP 443 and that the service is listening.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: You can diagnose connectivity by separating the route, address, and permissions, rather than relying only on the name or CIDR.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: If a subnet has an IGW route, all instances automatically become reachable from the internet.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: The instance also needs a public IPv4 address or an Elastic IP, along with the required communication permissions.

blocks.label: Key takeaway
blocks.text: Public accessibility is a combination of route tables, addresses, and permissions.

blocks.label: Key takeaway
blocks.text: A subnet name is not evidence of reachability.
